modeSub.rua: The cars you've caught on the street, from Common to Unicorn. Only cars that are driving or parked count: museums, shows, races and festivals go in the other logbook. Club team buses count when they're on the move.
modeSub.expo: Cars seen at museums, shows, races, festivals and meets. Almost everything here is special, so the scale is tougher than the street one.
modeSub.dex: Every car brand, like a Pokédex. A brand counts as caught when you have at least one of its cars, on the Street or at Shows.

rua.name: Common
rua.desc: You see loads of them every day.
rua.ex: Renault Clio, Peugeot 208, VW Golf, Opel Corsa

rua.name: Frequent
rua.desc: Seen a lot, just a bit less than the common ones.
rua.ex: Škoda Superb, Hyundai Tucson, BMW 3 Series, Tesla Model 3

rua.name: Uncommon
rua.desc: Turns up every now and then.
rua.ex: Mazda MX-5, Fiat 500 Abarth, Volvo 240, Mini Convertible

rua.name: Interesting
rua.desc: You make a point of taking a second look.
rua.ex: Ford Mustang, BMW Z4, Porsche Macan, a club's team bus

rua.name: Rare
rua.desc: You can go months without seeing one.
rua.ex: Renault Mégane CC, Renault Avantime, Fiat Coupé, classic Citroën DS

rua.name: Very rare
rua.desc: Proper sports cars and luxury cars.
rua.ex: Porsche Panamera, Porsche 911, Mercedes G-Class, Maserati

rua.name: Epic
rua.desc: The cars that stop the whole street.
rua.ex: Lamborghini Urus, Ferrari Roma, Bentley Continental, Porsche 911 GT3

rua.name: Legendary
rua.desc: Supercars. Maybe you'll see one a year.
rua.ex: Lamborghini Revuelto, Ferrari SF90, McLaren 750S, Rolls-Royce

rua.name: Mythic
rua.desc: Hypercars and ultra-rare classics out on the road.

rua.name: Unicorn
rua.desc: Almost impossible to catch on the street: one-of-a-kind cars or ones with only a handful made in the world.
rua.ex: Prototypes on test, one-offs, Ferrari 250 GTO, McLaren F1

expo.name: Common
expo.desc: Turns up at almost every show and event.
expo.ex: Beetle, classic Mini, Mustang, Camaro, classic Golf GTI

expo.name: Frequent
expo.desc: Well-kept popular classics and well-known sports cars.
expo.ex: Classic Fiat 500, Citroën 2CV, BMW M3, modern Porsche 911

expo.name: Uncommon
expo.desc: Less-seen classics and proper sports cars.
expo.ex: Classic Porsche 911, classic Mercedes SL, classic Alfa Romeo, military jeeps

expo.name: Interesting
expo.desc: You make a point of stopping for a closer look.
expo.ex: Tanks, rally cars, Lotus, rare muscle cars

expo.name: Very rare
expo.ex: Porsche GT4 RS and GT2 RS, Ferrari Pista, GT3 and Formula cars

expo.name: Epic
expo.desc: Valuable classics and very limited editions.
expo.ex: Mercedes 300 SL Gullwing, Lamborghini Miura, Lancia Stratos, Ferrari Daytona

expo.name: Legendary
expo.ex: Ferrari F40, McLaren P1, Porsche 918, championship-winning F1 cars

expo.name: Mythic
expo.desc: Ultra-rare pieces that few museums in the world have.
expo.ex: Bugatti, Pagani, Koenigsegg, Ferrari Enzo, McLaren F1

expo.name: Unicorn
expo.desc: One of a kind in the world.
expo.ex: Prototypes, concept cars, one-offs, Ferrari 250 GTO

facts.Abarth: The scorpion on the badge is the star sign of the founder, Carlo Abarth.
facts.Aixam: Makes licence-free microcars that you can drive from age 16.
facts.Alfa Romeo: The badge has a serpent, an old symbol of the city of Milan.
facts.Alpina: Turned BMWs into even faster and more comfortable cars.
facts.Alpine: Born winning rallies, and today it belongs to Renault.
facts.Audi: The four rings are four brands that joined together in 1932.
facts.Austin: Helped create the original Mini, in 1959.
facts.Bentley: Has won the 24 Hours of Le Mans six times.
facts.Brabus: Turns Mercedes into monsters with over 800 hp.
facts.Buick: One of the oldest American brands still going.
facts.BYD: Started out making mobile phone batteries.
facts.Cadillac: The name comes from the founder of the city of Detroit.
facts.Caterham: Makes the Seven, a super-light car inspired by a 1950s Lotus.
facts.Chery: One of the Chinese brands that exports the most cars.
facts.Chevrolet: Made the Corvette and the Camaro.
facts.Chrysler: Part of Stellantis, just like Peugeot and Fiat.
facts.Citroën: The badge is two gear teeth in a V shape.
facts.Cupra: It was SEAT's sporty version before becoming a brand of its own.
facts.Dacia: Belongs to Renault and makes some of the cheapest cars in Europe.
facts.Daewoo: Its models ended up being called Chevrolet.
facts.DAF: Makes lorries today, but made cars with automatic gearboxes back in the 50s.
facts.Daihatsu: Specialist in tiny cars. Left Europe in 2013.
facts.De Tomaso: The Pantera had an American Ford V8 engine.
facts.DeLorean: The car from the film Back to the Future, with gullwing doors.
facts.Dodge: Made the Viper and the Challenger.
facts.DS: The name comes from the famous 1955 Citroën DS.
facts.Ferrari: The prancing horse came from the plane of a First World War pilot.
facts.Fiat: The name stands for Italian Automobile Factory of Turin.
facts.Ford: Was the first to make cars on a moving assembly line.
facts.Gordon Murray: The T.50 has a giant fan at the back to suck the car to the ground.
facts.Hennessey: The Venom F5 was built to go past 480 km/h.
facts.Hispano-Suiza: An old luxury brand that came back with an electric hypercar.
facts.Honda: Started out putting engines on bicycles.
facts.Hummer: Born from the Humvee military vehicle and came back as an electric car.
facts.Ineos: Makes the Grenadier, inspired by the old Land Rover Defender.
facts.Isuzu: Makes the D-Max pickup and lots of lorries.
facts.Iveco: Makes the Daily van and lorries.
facts.Jaguar: The E-Type was called the most beautiful car in the world.
facts.Jeep: Born as a military jeep in the Second World War.
facts.Koenigsegg: The badge is the founder's family coat of arms.
facts.Lada: The Niva has been made almost unchanged since 1977.
facts.Lamborghini: Ferruccio Lamborghini made tractors before supercars.
facts.Lancia: The brand with the most World Rally Championship titles.
facts.Land Rover: They say the first model was drawn in the sand on a beach.
facts.Ligier: Once had a Formula 1 team. Today it makes licence-free microcars.
facts.Lincoln: American presidents rode in Lincolns for decades.
facts.Lotus: The founder's motto: simplify, then add lightness.
facts.Lucid: Makes some of the longest-range electric cars in the world.
facts.Lynk & Co: From the same group as Volvo. Started out selling cars by subscription.
facts.Mahindra: One of India's biggest makers of jeeps and tractors.
facts.MAN: Makes lorries and buses, like the Casa Pia team bus.
facts.Maserati: The trident comes from the statue of Neptune in Bologna.
facts.Maybach: Today it's Mercedes' top level of luxury.
facts.Mazda: The MX-5 is the best-selling roadster in history.
facts.McLaren: Started in Formula 1 and still races there.
facts.Mercedes-Benz: Karl Benz made the first car in history, in 1886.
facts.MG: It was British and today it's Chinese.
facts.Mini: The original Mini was only 3 metres long.
facts.Morgan: Still uses wood in the frame of its cars.
facts.NIO: Instead of charging, its cars can swap batteries in minutes.
facts.Omoda: A new brand from the Chery group.
facts.Peugeot: Before cars, it made pepper mills.
facts.Plymouth: An American brand that ended in 2001.
facts.Polestar: Started out as Volvo's performance division.
facts.Portaro: A 4x4 made in Portugal, based on a Romanian model.
facts.RAM: Giant pickups that grew out of Dodge.
facts.Renault: Won Formula 1 championships with Fernando Alonso.
facts.Rimac: The Nevera is one of the fastest electric cars in the world.
facts.Rivian: Electric pickups and SUVs built for adventure.
facts.Rolls-Royce: The statuette on the bonnet is called the Spirit of Ecstasy.
facts.Rover: A British brand that ended in 2005.
facts.Saab: Also made aeroplanes. Stopped making cars in 2011.
facts.Scania: The lorries with the griffin on the badge.
facts.Simca: A French brand that ended in 1978.
facts.Smart: The Fortwo is only 2.7 metres long.
facts.Subaru: The six stars on the badge are the Pleiades star cluster.
facts.Tesla: The name is a tribute to the inventor Nikola Tesla.
facts.Toyota: Also started out making looms, just like Suzuki.
facts.Trabant: The body was made of a plastic mixed with cotton.
facts.Triumph: Made roadsters like the Spitfire and the TR6.
facts.TVR: British sports cars famous for being wild.
facts.UMM: A Portuguese 4x4, used by the Army.
facts.Volvo: Invented the 3-point seatbelt and let everyone use it.
facts.Xpeng: Is also working on flying cars.
facts.Zeekr: From the same group as Volvo and Polestar.
facts.Zenvo: A Danish hypercar with a rear wing that tilts in corners.
facts.GWM: In Europe the Ora 03 was called Funky Cat, and in China, Good Cat.
facts.Geely: It started out making fridge parts and now owns Volvo.
facts.Jaecoo: The name mixes the German word Jäger (hunter) with the English word cool.
facts.Maxus: The name comes from a British van, the LDV Maxus.
facts.Microcar: It was born inside a company that built sailing boats.
facts.Vauxhall: The name comes from the London district where the company was born.
facts.Holden: The lion on the badge holds a stone, because of a legend about the invention of the wheel.
facts.Proton: The name is an acronym for National Automobile Company in Malay.
facts.VinFast: Its first models used BMW platforms and engines.
facts.Ariel: The Atom has no roof, doors or windows: you can see the whole chassis.
facts.Noble: The M600 switches off traction control with a switch like the one in a fighter jet.
facts.Spyker: The badge combines an aircraft propeller and a spoked wheel.
facts.SSC: The founder is called Shelby, but he is not related to Carroll Shelby, the Cobra man.
facts.Czinger: Many parts are 3D-printed and the driver sits in the middle, with the passenger behind.
facts.W Motors: The Lykan HyperSport's headlights have diamonds in them.

hist.Abarth: Founded in Turin by Carlo Abarth, an Austrian who loved speed. It became famous for turning small Fiats into race cars and won thousands of races in the 50s and 60s. It has belonged to Fiat since 1971 and today makes the spiciest versions of the 500.
hist.Acura: Created by Honda in 1986 to sell luxury cars in the USA. It was the first Japanese luxury brand. Its most famous model is the NSX, which racing driver Ayrton Senna helped with while it was being developed.
hist.Aixam: A French brand specialising in quadricycles, the so-called licence-free cars. In Portugal they can be driven from age 16. It's one of the best-selling brands of this type of car in Europe.
hist.Alfa Romeo: Born in Milan in 1910 as A.L.F.A., and the Romeo came from Nicola Romeo, who bought the company. It won the first Formula 1 World Championship, in 1950. Enzo Ferrari began his career as a driver and team manager for Alfa Romeo.
hist.Alpina: Started out making parts to improve BMW engines and became a small luxury and performance brand. The cars are built with BMW, but have multi-spoke wheels and special interiors. In 2022 BMW itself bought the brand.
hist.Alpine: Founded by Jean Rédélé in Dieppe, France. The 70s A110 won the first World Rally Championship, in 1973. After years out of action, Renault brought the brand back in 2017 with a new A110.
hist.Aston Martin: The name combines Lionel Martin, one of the founders, and the Aston Hill climb, where he raced. It became world-famous when the DB5 appeared in the James Bond film Goldfinger, in 1964. Today it also has a Formula 1 team.
hist.Audi: Audi is the Latin translation of Horch, the founder's surname, and means 'listen!'. In 1932 it joined DKW, Horch and Wanderer to form Auto Union, hence the four rings. In the 80s it revolutionised rallying with quattro all-wheel drive.
hist.Austin: Founded by Herbert Austin in England. The little Austin Seven, from the 1920s, got lots of British families driving. Later it joined other brands in the British Motor Corporation and helped launch the Mini, in 1959.
hist.Bentley: Founded by W. O. Bentley in London. In the 1920s, the drivers known as the 'Bentley Boys' won Le Mans several times in a row. It was bought by Rolls-Royce in 1931 and today belongs to the Volkswagen Group.
hist.BMW: BMW stands for Bavarian Motor Works. It started with aircraft engines, then motorbikes, and only made its first car in 1928. The blue and white badge has the colours of the Bavarian flag.
hist.Brabus: A German tuner from Bottrop, specialising in Mercedes and Smart. It takes production cars and gives them much more powerful engines and luxury interiors. Brabus G-Classes are some of the most over-the-top 4x4s in the world.
hist.Bugatti: Founded by the Italian Ettore Bugatti in Molsheim, a town that is now in France. The 1920s Type 35 won more than a thousand races. The brand was reborn with the Veyron, in 2005, the first production car with over 1000 hp.
hist.Buick: Founded by David Buick, a Scotsman living in the USA. General Motors was created from Buick, in 1908. Today it sells mainly in the USA and China.
hist.BYD: The name stands for 'Build Your Dreams'. It started out making batteries and moved into cars in 2003. Today it's the world's biggest maker of electric and plug-in hybrid cars.
hist.Cadillac: Born in Detroit from Henry Ford's old company, after he had left it. It has belonged to General Motors since 1909. The Escalade is the favourite car of lots of American rappers and sports stars.
hist.Caterham: In 1973 it bought the rights to the Lotus Seven, a car from 1957. Since then it has kept making the Seven, faster and faster but always light and simple. Many customers build their own car from a kit.
hist.Chery: A Chinese brand from Wuhu, created with the support of the local government. For many years it was the Chinese brand that exported the most cars. In Europe it sells cars under the Omoda and Jaecoo brands.
hist.Chevrolet: Founded by Louis Chevrolet, a Swiss racing driver, and William Durant, the creator of General Motors. The Corvette, from 1953, is the most famous American sports car. It's one of the brands that has sold the most cars in history.
hist.Chrysler: Founded by Walter Chrysler, who used to work at Buick. For decades it was one of Detroit's 'Big Three', with Ford and GM. Today it's part of Stellantis.
hist.Citroën: André Citroën was the first in Europe to mass-produce cars, like Ford did in the USA. He created very innovative cars, like the Traction Avant, the 2CV and the DS with hydraulic suspension. The badge comes from the V-shaped gears the company made before cars.
hist.Cupra: The name comes from 'Cup Racing', SEAT's racing versions. In 2018 it became an independent brand, based in Martorell, Spain. The Formentor was the first model made just for Cupra.
hist.Dacia: A Romanian brand that started out making Renaults under licence. It was bought by Renault in 1999 and launched the Logan, a simple, cheap car. Today the Sandero is one of the best-selling cars in Europe.
hist.Daewoo: It was part of a huge Korean group that also built ships and electronics. It went bust in the Asian financial crisis and General Motors bought the car side in 2002. From then on, its models wore the Chevrolet badge.
hist.DAF: A Dutch brand from Eindhoven that made small cars with a belt-driven automatic gearbox, the Variomatic. The car side went to Volvo in the 70s. Today it makes only lorries and belongs to the American company PACCAR.
hist.Daihatsu: Claims to be the oldest Japanese car brand still in business. It specialises in tiny cars, Japanese kei cars. It belongs to Toyota and left Europe in 2013.
hist.De Tomaso: Founded in Modena by the Argentinian Alejandro de Tomaso. The Pantera combined Italian style with a Ford V8 engine, and was sold at Ford dealers in the USA. The brand recently came back with the P72.
hist.DeLorean: Created by John DeLorean, who had been a big boss at General Motors. It made just one model, the DMC-12, with an unpainted stainless steel body. The factory, in Northern Ireland, closed in 1982, but the car became famous thanks to the film Back to the Future.
hist.Dodge: Founded by the brothers John and Horace Dodge, who made parts for Ford. It became famous for muscle cars, like the Charger and the Challenger. Today it's part of Stellantis.
hist.DS: Started as Citroën's luxury line and became a brand of its own in 2014. The name honours the Citroën DS, one of the most advanced cars of its time. It's the brand used by the presidents of France.
hist.Ferrari: Enzo Ferrari started out as a driver and team manager for Alfa Romeo. He created Scuderia Ferrari in 1929, and the first car with the Ferrari name came out in 1947. It's the oldest and most successful team in Formula 1.
hist.Fiat: Founded in Turin by a group of investors, including Giovanni Agnelli. The 1957 Fiat 500 got the whole of Italy driving. Today it's part of Stellantis.
hist.Ford: Henry Ford founded the brand in Detroit. The Model T, from 1908, was the first car cheap enough for lots of families. In 1966 the GT40 won Le Mans ahead of Ferrari, a story that was made into a film.
hist.Genesis: Started as the name of a Hyundai luxury model. In 2015 it became a brand of its own. It competes with Mercedes, BMW and Audi.
hist.Gordon Murray: Gordon Murray designed championship-winning Formula 1 cars and the legendary McLaren F1. At his own brand he makes light supercars with a manual gearbox and a V12 engine. The T.50 is seen as the successor to the McLaren F1.
hist.Hennessey: A Texas tuner that started out modifying other brands' cars. The Venom GT was based on a Lotus Exige. It then created the Venom F5, built from scratch to be one of the fastest cars in the world.
hist.Hispano-Suiza: A Spanish brand founded in Barcelona with the help of a Swiss engineer, hence the name. It made luxury cars and famous aircraft engines in the First World War. It came back in 2019 with the Carmen, an electric hypercar.
hist.Honda: Soichiro Honda started out putting engines on bicycles after the Second World War. It became the world's biggest motorbike maker. In Formula 1 it won titles with Ayrton Senna and, later, with Max Verstappen.
hist.Hongqi: The name means 'red flag'. It's one of China's oldest car brands and made the limousines for the country's leaders. Today it also sells electric SUVs in Europe.
hist.Hummer: Born from the Humvee, the American military vehicle. The first civilian Hummers came out in 1992 and General Motors bought the brand, which closed in 2010. It came back as the Hummer EV, an electric giant sold by GMC.
hist.Hyundai: Founded by businessman Chung Ju-yung, who also created giant shipyards and construction companies. The Pony, from 1975, was the first car mass-produced in Korea. Today it's one of the biggest brands in the world, together with Kia, which belongs to the same group.
hist.Ineos: Created by British billionaire Jim Ratcliffe, owner of a large chemicals company. When the old Land Rover Defender ended, he decided to make a similar 4x4: the Grenadier. The name comes from a London pub where the idea came up.
hist.Infiniti: Nissan's luxury brand, created for the USA in 1989. It sponsored Red Bull in Formula 1 when Sebastian Vettel was champion. It left Europe in 2020.
hist.Isuzu: One of Japan's oldest brands, specialising in diesel engines. It makes very tough lorries and pickups. In Portugal it's known for the D-Max pickup.
hist.Iveco: Born in 1975 from the merger of several European lorry brands, with Fiat. The name stands for Industrial Vehicles Corporation. The Daily van is one of the most used in Portugal.
hist.Jaguar: Started out making sidecars for motorbikes, under the name Swallow. The Jaguar C-Type and D-Type won Le Mans in the 1950s. It has belonged to India's Tata since 2008.
hist.Jeep: Born from the Willys MB, the American military jeep of the Second World War. The Portuguese word 'jipe' comes from it. Today it's part of Stellantis.
hist.Kia: Korea's oldest car brand. It started out making bicycle parts and then motorbikes. It has belonged to the Hyundai group since 1998.
hist.Koenigsegg: Christian von Koenigsegg founded the brand when he was just 22, to build the perfect car. The factory is on a former Swedish Air Force base. Several Koenigseggs have set speed records.
hist.Lada: The brand of the AvtoVAZ factory, in Togliatti, Russia. The first models were based on the Fiat 124. The Niva was one of the world's first SUVs with a monocoque body.
hist.Lamborghini: Ferruccio Lamborghini got rich making tractors. The story goes that, after an argument with Enzo Ferrari, he decided to make better cars than his. The Miura and the Countach invented the supercar look. Today it belongs to the Volkswagen Group.
hist.Lancia: Founded by Vincenzo Lancia, who was a Fiat racing driver. In rallying it was unbeatable with the Stratos, the 037 and the Delta Integrale. Today it's part of Stellantis and is being reborn with the new Ypsilon.
hist.Land Rover: Created after the Second World War to make a farm vehicle similar to the Jeep. The first ones were made of aluminium because steel was scarce. The Range Rover, from 1970, was one of the first luxury SUVs.
hist.Leapmotor: A Chinese startup from Hangzhou that makes affordable electric cars. In 2023 Stellantis bought a stake in the company. That's why, in Europe, Leapmotors are sold through the Stellantis group.
hist.Lexus: Created by Toyota in 1989 to sell luxury cars in the USA. In a famous advert, the first LS was so smooth that a pyramid of glasses stayed balanced on the bonnet with the engine running. The LFA is one of the best-sounding supercars ever.
hist.Ligier: Guy Ligier was a rugby player, racing driver and owner of a Formula 1 team. The team won several races in the 70s and 80s. Today the brand makes licence-free microcars.
hist.Lincoln: Founded by Henry Leland, the same man who had created Cadillac. It was bought by Ford in 1922. For decades it made the cars of American presidents.
hist.Lotus: Colin Chapman founded Lotus and revolutionised Formula 1 with light cars full of new ideas. The Lotus team won 7 constructors' championships. Today it belongs to the Chinese Geely group.
hist.Lucid: Founded in the USA, with engineers who came from Tesla. The Lucid Air can do more than 800 km on a single charge. A large part of the company belongs to a Saudi Arabian fund.
hist.Lynk & Co: A brand from the Geely group, the same as Volvo, created in 2016. In Europe it started with a monthly subscription system, like a mobile phone contract. The cars share a lot of technology with Volvo.
hist.Mahindra: A big Indian group that started out assembling Willys jeeps. It's the world's biggest tractor maker. It also has a team in Formula E.
hist.MAN: One of Germany's oldest industrial companies. It was there that Rudolf Diesel built the first working diesel engine. Today it makes lorries and buses and belongs to the Volkswagen Group.
hist.Maserati: Founded in Bologna by the Maserati brothers, who made race cars. Juan Manuel Fangio became Formula 1 world champion in a Maserati, in 1957. Today it's part of Stellantis.
hist.Maybach: Wilhelm Maybach was the great engineer behind the first Mercedes. His son, Karl, made luxury cars and engines for Zeppelin airships. Today Maybach is the most luxurious level of Mercedes-Benz.
hist.Mazda: Started out making cork and then three-wheeled trucks. It's famous for the rotary engine, used in the RX-7 and RX-8. In 1991 it was the first Japanese brand to win the 24 Hours of Le Mans.
hist.McLaren: Bruce McLaren, a driver from New Zealand, founded the racing team. McLaren is one of the most successful teams in Formula 1, with drivers like Senna, Prost and Hamilton. The 1992 McLaren F1 was the fastest car in the world for years.
hist.Mercedes-Benz: Karl Benz made the first car in 1886 and Gottlieb Daimler made another at almost the same time. The two companies merged in 1926. The name Mercedes comes from the daughter of Emil Jellinek, an important customer.
hist.MG: MG stands for Morris Garages, an Oxford workshop that made sporty versions of Morris cars. It became famous for British roadsters like the MGB. Today it belongs to China's SAIC and is one of the fastest-growing brands in Europe.
hist.Mini: The original Mini was designed by Alec Issigonis to use very little fuel. It won the Monte Carlo Rally three times in the 60s. The brand has belonged to BMW since 2001.
hist.Mitsubishi: Part of a big Japanese group that also builds ships and aircraft. It won the Dakar Rally 12 times with the Pajero and the World Rally Championship with the Lancer Evolution. It's part of an alliance with Renault and Nissan.
hist.Morgan: A family-run English brand that still makes its cars almost by hand. It started with three-wheelers. It still uses ash wood in the frame today.
hist.NIO: A Chinese startup from Shanghai, created in 2014. It has stations where a robot swaps the car's battery in a few minutes. The EP9 set records at the Nürburgring.
hist.Nissan: The name comes from Nippon Sangyo. For years it sold cars under the Datsun name. The GT-R won so many races in Japan that it was nicknamed Godzilla.
hist.Omoda: A brand created by Chery in 2022 to sell cars outside China, mainly in Europe. Its models have a futuristic style. It's already on sale in Portugal.
hist.Opel: Adam Opel started out making sewing machines and then bicycles. For many years it belonged to America's General Motors. Since 2017 it has been in the same group as Peugeot, now called Stellantis.
hist.Pagani: Horacio Pagani, an Argentinian, worked at Lamborghini before creating his own brand. It makes carbon fibre hypercars almost by hand. Every car has hundreds of titanium bolts engraved with the logo.
hist.Peugeot: The Peugeot family made tools, coffee and pepper mills, and bicycles. It's considered the oldest car brand in the world still in business. It has won the Dakar and the 24 Hours of Le Mans several times.
hist.Plymouth: It was the cheapest brand in the Chrysler group. It made some of the most famous muscle cars, like the Road Runner and the Hemi Cuda. It ended in 2001.
hist.Polestar: Started out as a racing team that tuned Volvos. Volvo bought it and turned it into a brand of sporty electric cars. It belongs to the Geely group.
hist.Pontiac: A General Motors brand with a sporty reputation. The 1964 GTO is considered the first muscle car. The car from Knight Rider, KITT, was a Pontiac Firebird Trans Am.
hist.Porsche: Ferdinand Porsche designed the Volkswagen Beetle before creating his own brand. The first Porsche, the 356, came out in 1948. Porsche is the brand with the most wins at the 24 Hours of Le Mans.
hist.Portaro: A 4x4 built in Portugal based on the Romanian ARO, with diesel engines. The name combines Portugal and ARO. It was made from the 70s to the early 90s.
hist.RAM: It was the name of Dodge's pickups and became a brand of its own in 2010. The RAM 1500 is one of the best-selling pickups in the USA. In Portugal they're rare because they're enormous.
hist.Renault: Founded by the brothers Louis, Marcel and Fernand Renault. In Formula 1 it won titles with Williams and with Fernando Alonso. In Portugal, the Clio was the best-selling car for many years.
hist.Rimac: Mate Rimac started making electric cars in a garage in Croatia. The Nevera has almost 2000 hp. The company took control of Bugatti, in partnership with Porsche.
hist.Rivian: An American startup making electric vehicles built for adventure. Amazon invested in the company and uses Rivian electric vans for deliveries. The R1T was the first electric pickup to hit the road.
hist.Rolls-Royce: Charles Rolls and Henry Royce teamed up in 1906. The brand became known for making 'the best car in the world'. Since 2003 the cars have been made by BMW, in Goodwood, England.
hist.Rover: Started out making bicycles in Coventry, England. It was Rover that created the first Land Rover, which later became a brand of its own. It ended in 2005.
hist.Saab: A Swedish fighter-plane maker that started making cars after the Second World War. It was a pioneer in putting turbo engines in ordinary cars. It closed in 2011.
hist.Scania: A Swedish lorry and bus brand from Södertälje. Scania lorries with V8 engines are famous among truckers. It belongs to the Volkswagen Group.
hist.SEAT: Created by the Spanish government to make Fiat cars under licence, like the SEAT 600. It has belonged to the Volkswagen Group since 1986. The main factory is in Martorell, near Barcelona.
hist.Simca: Started out making Fiat cars in France. In the 60s it was one of the biggest French brands. It ended up absorbed by Chrysler and then by Peugeot.
hist.Škoda: Founded by Václav Laurin and Václav Klement, who made bicycles and motorbikes. It's one of the oldest car brands in the world. It was bought by Volkswagen in 1991.
hist.Smart: Born from an idea by Mercedes with Swatch, the watch brand. The name combines Swatch, Mercedes and Art. Today it's a partnership between Mercedes and China's Geely.
hist.SsangYong: A Korean brand specialising in 4x4s and SUVs. For a few years it made cars with Mercedes engines. In 2023 it changed its name to KGM.
hist.Subaru: A brand from the group that also makes aircraft and helicopters in Japan. The blue and yellow Impreza won the World Rally Championship with Colin McRae. Almost every Subaru has a boxer engine and all-wheel drive.
hist.Suzuki: Michio Suzuki made looms for weaving fabric. He then moved on to motorbikes and small cars. The Jimny is one of the most capable small 4x4s in the world.
hist.Tata: A huge Indian group that makes everything from steel to tea. The Tata Nano was launched as the cheapest car in the world. In 2008 it bought Jaguar and Land Rover.
hist.Tesla: Founded in 2003 by American engineers, with Elon Musk as the big investor and later the boss. The first model was a Roadster based on the Lotus Elise. It helped make electric cars popular all over the world.
hist.Toyota: Started out making automatic looms, invented by Sakichi Toyoda. It's the biggest car maker in the world. The Corolla is the best-selling car in history.
hist.Trabant: It was made in the old East Germany, in communist times. People waited more than 10 years to get one. It had a very noisy two-stroke engine.
hist.Triumph: Started out making bicycles and motorbikes in Coventry, England. It became famous for cheap sporty roadsters. The car brand ended in 1984.
hist.TVR: Founded by Trevor Wilkinson in Blackpool, England; the name comes from TreVoR. It made light sports cars with huge engines and no electronic aids. It's trying to come back with a new Griffith.
hist.UMM: UMM stands for União Metalo-Mecânica, a Portuguese company. It made tough 4x4s based on a French model, used by the Army and by lots of companies. They were also sold to other countries.
hist.Volkswagen: Created in Germany to make a cheap car for everyone, the Beetle, which sold more than 21 million. Today the Volkswagen Group owns Audi, Porsche, Lamborghini, Bentley, SEAT, Cupra and Škoda. In Portugal, the Palmela factory makes the T-Roc.
hist.Volvo: Volvo means 'I roll' in Latin. It became famous for safety, and it was a Volvo engineer who invented the 3-point seatbelt. Today it belongs to China's Geely.
hist.Xpeng: A Chinese startup from Guangzhou, specialising in technology and self-driving. It has a sister company developing flying cars. Volkswagen has invested in the brand.
hist.Zeekr: A luxury electric car brand from the Geely group, created in 2021. It uses the same technical base as some Volvos and Polestars. It's already on sale in several European countries.
hist.Zenvo: A small Danish brand that makes very few cars a year. The TSR-S's rear wing tilts sideways in corners. The Aurora has a quad-turbo V12 engine.
hist.GWM: Great Wall Motor was born in Baoding, China, and by 1984 it was already making small trucks and off-roaders. It became famous for pickups, like the 1996 Deer, and grew into China's biggest pickup maker. Today it brings together several brands: Haval (SUVs), Wey (premium), ORA (electric) and Tank (off-road).
hist.Geely: It was founded in 1986 by Li Shufu, who started out making fridge parts. Its first car, the Haoqing, left the factory in 1998, and in 2010 Geely bought Volvo. Today the group includes brands such as Lotus, Polestar, Zeekr and Lynk & Co, and it arrived in Portugal in 2026.
hist.Jaecoo: It is a brand from the Chinese Chery group, launched in 2023 and designed mainly for export. It is Omoda's sister brand and specialises in adventurous-looking SUVs. Its first model was the Jaecoo 7, which also comes as a plug-in hybrid.
hist.Maxus: In 2010 China's SAIC bought the rights to the British company LDV, which made work vans. Maxus was born in 2011 and builds vans, pickups and people carriers. It is one of the brands pushing hardest into electric work vans, like the eDeliver range.
hist.Microcar: It was created in 1980 as a division of Jeanneau, a French sailing boat maker. It specialised in quadricycles, the licence-free cars that in Portugal can be driven from age 16. Since 2008 it has belonged to Ligier, another French maker of licence-free cars.
hist.Vauxhall: It was born in London in 1857 making pumps and marine engines, and built its first car in 1903. In 1925 it was bought by General Motors, which also owned Opel. Since 1980 Vauxhalls have been almost identical to Opels, but with right-hand drive and a griffin on the badge.
hist.Holden: It started in 1856 in Adelaide, Australia, making horse saddles, and became part of General Motors in 1931. In 1948 it launched the 48-215, the first car to carry the Holden name, and later created icons like the Monaro and the Commodore. It won the Bathurst race more times than any other brand, but closed its factory in 2017 and the brand ended in 2021.
hist.Proton: It was created in Malaysia in 1983, the idea of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, so the country would have its own car. The first model, the Saga, appeared in 1985 and was based on a Mitsubishi. It owned Lotus from 1996 to 2017, and today China's Geely owns almost half the company.
hist.VinFast: It was founded in 2017 by the Vingroup group, with a factory in Hai Phong, Vietnam. It showed its first cars at the 2018 Paris Motor Show, based on BMW models. In 2022 it stopped making combustion cars and switched to electric only, like the small VF 3.
hist.Ariel: It was founded in 1991 by Simon Saunders in Crewkerne, UK, and revived the name of an old British brand. The Atom began as a Coventry University project, created by Saunders and a student, and went into production in 2000. It is a small company of about 30 people that also makes the Nomad, an off-roader with no bodywork.
hist.Noble: It was founded in 1999 by Briton Lee Noble in Leeds and is now based in Leicester, UK. It became famous for the M12, a light sports car with a twin-turbo V6. The M600, on sale since 2010, has a twin-turbo V8 with about 650 horsepower and almost no electronic driving aids.
hist.Spyker: The name comes from a Dutch brand founded in 1880 by the Spijker brothers, which built the royal family's Golden Coach and later cars and aeroplanes. Today's Spyker was born in 1999 and became known for the C8 supercar. It once had a Formula 1 team in 2007 and bought Saab in 2010, but went through several bankruptcies.
hist.SSC: It was founded in 1998 by Jerod Shelby in Washington State, USA, under the name Shelby SuperCars. In 2007 Guinness confirmed the Ultimate Aero as the world's fastest production car, at about 412 km/h. In 2021 the Tuatara averaged 455 km/h on the old Space Shuttle runway at the Kennedy Space Center.
hist.Czinger: It was founded in 2019 in Los Angeles, USA, by Kevin Czinger and his son Lukas. The 21C was unveiled in 2020 and uses many computer-designed, 3D-printed parts. Only 80 will be built, and it has already set records at tracks like Laguna Seca.
hist.W Motors: It was founded in 2012 in Beirut, Lebanon, by Ralph Debbas, and soon moved to Dubai. Its first model, the Lykan HyperSport, is billed as the first Arab hypercar, and only 7 were made. It appeared in the film Furious 7, and the Abu Dhabi police bought one too.
